text:
Mira: Quick question — should we standardize on operator-bridge or direct service-claims for cross-tenant workers? hitting tradeoffs around intent scoping and isolation.
Juan: We saw this with the batch importer. Direct claims are simpler (no broker) but they expose org context to downstreams. operator-bridge isolates tenant context but adds latency and an extra TTLed token.
Alex: Proposal idea: operator-bridge for public/multi-tenant-facing routes; direct claims allowed for internal-only services behind mesh. Anyone object?
Kevin: Main tradeoffs: authz surface growth, telemetry continuity, rotation complexity. Operator adds broker and TTL churn. Direct requires stricter role mappings and better key hygiene.
devops-bot: deploy 2025-06-18T14:22:11Z: operator-bridge v2 staged to canary (no errors)
Sam: If we add "intent" claims (eg `intent:embedding:create`) that narrows RBAC checks a lot. Example JWT payload we discussed:
```json
{"sub":"svc-importer","org":"org-123","intent":"batch:ingest","exp":1710000000}
```
Juan: SDKs will need to validate intent on the client side too. Migration plan: accept legacy keys for 6 months and default-route them through operator-bridge when org context needs hiding.
Alex: Edge case: background workers that process mixed-org streams — operator-bridge forces ephemeral operator tokens per-item which increases ops cost and request overhead.
Mira: Could we support a hybrid? operator-bridge for cross-org requests and direct claims for pinned, single-tenant routes. Make routing a gateway policy.
Kevin: Also watch billing/rate-limits: operator tokens must carry both `subject` and `origin_org` to attribute quota/billing correctly; otherwise billing gets fuzzy.
Sam: Actionable: I'll draft a mini-RFC with config examples and a migration timeline and ping infra for proxy hooks. @Kevin @Juan please review when ready.
Kevin: SGTM. +1 :thumbsup: @Sam please include a sample NGINX Lua header-rewrite snippet for the gateway.
Juan: :eyes: I'll compile a service list that should remain direct-claims (low-latency, single-tenant).
Mira: Thanks all — sounds like we have a direction. Will wait for the mini-RFC and then we can slot a meeting if needed.
